business: MYTHRI (AI Emotional Support & Mental Health Companion)
why_not: I'm not willing to entrust my private mental health struggles to an AI app when I don't know where the data really ends up, and a chatbot can't offer real human care.

I've already cycled through and abandoned Calm and journaling apps, and I just don't believe an AI chatbot simulating empathy can actually support me when I'm overwhelmed by work deadlines. It feels like a robotic substitute rather than genuine care.
I already turn to free ChatGPT on my phone when I get anxious and need to vent late at night. On a student budget, I can't justify paying a monthly subscription for something I already get for free.

I always lose steam and abandon self-care apps within four days, so putting down payment info for another subscription feels pointless. Without established Reddit threads or reviews proving long-term retention, I know I'd just waste my money.

I only make about $16,000 a year as a student, so taking on another recurring subscription isn't realistic for my budget. When I'm spiraling late at night I'd love support, but I can't justify paying $10 a month when money is this tight.

As a college student making $18,000 a year, $9.99 a month is way too steep for an app I might abandon like Calm or Headspace. Even the launch promo feels like another subscription trap when I can just vent to free AI tools.
I want real professional therapy, and an AI chatbot feels too synthetic and shallow to actually help when I'm dealing with complex emotions.

I would sign up for the free trial, but I'd likely cancel before being charged because I expect an AI companion to offer superficial platitudes rather than deep coping support. When I am overwhelmed by work deadlines, generic or hallucinated advice would just frustrate me more.
I already have ChatGPT and Claude open all day while working, and they listen to me vent for free. Plus, I always end up abandoning wellness app subscriptions after a couple of weeks anyway.

I can already vent to free ChatGPT or Claude late at night, so I see no reason to pay a recurring subscription. Without established Reddit threads or app store reviews proving it's meaningfully better, I'm definitely not entering my credit card.
